name: Thrust-vector-control (TVC) actuators (merchant tier)
description: Electromechanical / electrohydraulic / electrohydrostatic actuators that gimbal launch-vehicle engine nozzles for steering. On SpaceX engines this function is captive: Merlin uses hydraulic pistons driven by the engine's own RP-1 turbopump pressure, and Super Heavy's gimbaling Raptors switched from hydraulic to an in-house electric actuation system after Starship flight 1. The genuine merchant TVC-actuator tier (Moog, Woodward) flies on OTHER programs (ULA Vulcan/Centaur, Antares, SLS-class upper stages), not on SpaceX engine cores.
notes: Captive-vs-merchant honesty: SpaceX engine TVC actuation is overwhelmingly in-house (Merlin fuel-pressure hydraulics; Super Heavy all-electric since 2023). Merchant actuator suppliers below are flight-proven on non-SpaceX reusable/expendable programs and represent the supply tier any reusable-launch program that does NOT vertically integrate would buy from. Single-source character: no public merchant supplies SpaceX's gimbal actuators; that corner is captive.

name: Propellant & pneumatic control valves (merchant tier)
description: Cryogenic-compatible propellant and pressurant control valves (ball, poppet, pilot-operated), engine control valves, and pneumatic/servo valves for launch-vehicle engines and stage fluid systems. Merchant suppliers (Moog, Woodward, Parker Aerospace, Eaton) sell these across the launch industry; SpaceX builds much of its own valve set in-house for Merlin/Raptor but the broader reusable-launch industry draws on this merchant tier.
notes: Merchant tier is real and multi-source for valves (Moog, Woodward, Parker, Eaton) — unlike actuators this is NOT a single-source corner. SpaceX-specific valve sourcing is not publicly disclosed and is substantially captive; the suppliers here are mapped at industry altitude (qualified across launch programs), not asserted as SpaceX's specific vendors.

name: Engine igniters / ignition systems
description: Spark-torch / augmented-spark igniters that light the main combustion chamber and preburner/gas-generator of liquid rocket engines. SpaceX uses in-house torch igniters on Merlin and a spark-ignition system on Raptor; no public merchant igniter supplier to SpaceX was found. This component is documented as genuinely captive at SpaceX with only a thin/absent public merchant tier for reusable-launch primes.
notes: GENUINELY CAPTIVE / no merchant source found: round-1 search surfaced only patent literature and prime-internal torch/spark igniter designs (SpaceX, NASA, Blue Origin), no merchant catalog igniter supplier to SpaceX. Honest miss recorded rather than a fabricated supplier. Woodward markets monopropellant/cold-gas valves and some ignition-adjacent controls for satellites but not a confirmed launch-engine igniter to SpaceX.

name: Precision bearings (engine turbopump / gimbal / cryogenic)
description: Precision rolling-element, spherical, and cryogenic self-lubricating bearings for engine turbopumps, gimbal/thrust-vector joints, and stage mechanisms in launch vehicles. Merchant bearing makers (RBC Bearings with flight-proven cryogenic FibriloidCR bearings for Space Launch Vehicle applications; Schaeffler; SKF) serve this tier; turbopump-internal bearings on SpaceX engines are not publicly sourced and are likely captive/custom.
notes: RBC's FibriloidCR is the cleanest named launch-vehicle bearing product (cryogenic, flight-proven for Space Launch Vehicle & satellite applications). Schaeffler/SKF are general precision-bearing majors reused from the parcel/bearing domain; their specific launch-engine turbopump bearing role is qualitative (industry-capability), not a confirmed SpaceX turbopump supply.

name: Metal additive-manufacturing machines (engine parts)
description: Laser powder-bed fusion (LPBF / DMLS) and large-format metal 3D-printing machines used to print rocket-engine hot-section and propulsion parts (injectors/injector heads, manifolds, combustion-chamber and turbopump components). SpaceX prints Raptor/Merlin parts on Velo3D Sapphire systems under a Sept-2024 licensing deal; EOS and Nikon SLM Solutions supply DMLS/LPBF machines used across the reusable-rocket-engine industry (ArianeGroup, Rocket Lab, LEAP 71).
notes: This is the one engine-adjacent component with a CONFIRMED SpaceX merchant supplier: Velo3D Sapphire printers in use at SpaceX for Raptor parts (2024-09-12 licensing deal). EOS (private) and Nikon SLM Solutions (Nikon subsidiary) are merchant LPBF machine suppliers to the broader reusable-rocket-engine industry; their direct SpaceX use is not publicly confirmed (reported_capable_supplier altitude).

name: Metal AM powder & specialty alloy feedstock (engine parts)
description: Aerospace-grade metal powders (nickel/cobalt/titanium superalloys; copper alloys for regen-cooled combustion-chamber liners) and specialty-alloy feedstock for additively manufactured and forged rocket-engine parts. Merchant suppliers include Carpenter Additive (Carpenter Technology) and ATI. SpaceX's GRCop-class copper liner alloy is NASA-developed and substantially captive/internally produced; the merchant powder tier supplies the wider engine-AM industry.
notes: Honesty on the hot-section: the GRCop-42/84 copper-alloy combustion-chamber liner used on Raptor/Merlin is a NASA-Glenn-developed alloy that SpaceX produces largely in-house — NOT a merchant purchase. Carpenter Additive (Ni/Co/Ti powders) and ATI (Ti + Ni superalloy powder for AM) are genuine merchant powder suppliers to the broader aerospace-engine AM market; treated as industry-capability suppliers, not confirmed SpaceX feedstock vendors.

name: Moog Inc.
description: U.S. precision-motion-control supplier; designs and manufactures launch-vehicle thrust-vector-control actuators (electromechanical, electrohydraulic, electrohydrostatic) and cryogenic propellant/pressurant control valves. Flight-proven TVC actuators on ULA Vulcan first stage, Antares first stage, Centaur and Ares upper stages — i.e. the merchant TVC tier for reusable/expendable launch programs other than SpaceX (whose engine actuation is captive).
notes: Ticker MOG.A (NYSE) verified 2026-06 via NYSE/Nasdaq listings (also MOG.B class B). Merchant relevance: TVC actuators + cryogenic engine control valves; flies on Vulcan/Antares/Centaur/Ares, not on SpaceX Merlin/Raptor (captive). listingStatus public.

name: Woodward, Inc.
description: U.S. control-systems supplier (Fort Collins, CO). Its Space & Defense business supplies launch-vehicle main-engine controls, thrust-vector-control actuation, flight-control actuation, control valves and servo valves, plus satellite monopropellant/cold-gas valves and gimbal actuation — a merchant actuation/valve tier for the launch industry.
notes: Ticker WWD (NASDAQ) verified 2026-06 via Woodward IR / exchange. Merchant relevance: TVC actuation + control/servo valves for launch vehicles; not a confirmed SpaceX engine-core supplier. listingStatus public.

name: Parker Hannifin Corporation (Parker Aerospace)
description: U.S. motion-and-control major; Parker Aerospace supplies engine fuel/lubrication/thermal-management systems, hydraulics, fluid-management, and aerospace valves for missiles, rockets and launch vehicles (e.g. NASA SLS and Orion; historical Space Shuttle and Apollo propellant-feed valves). Merchant fluid-systems/valve tier for launch.
notes: Ticker PH (NYSE) verified 2026-06 via Parker IR (investors.parker.com) / exchange. Merchant relevance: launch-vehicle fuel/fluid systems and valves (SLS/Orion named); SpaceX-specific role not disclosed. listingStatus public.

name: Velo3D, Inc.
description: U.S. metal additive-manufacturing OEM (Sapphire laser powder-bed-fusion systems for support-free complex metal parts). SpaceX uses Velo3D Sapphire printers to produce engine components including Raptor parts; in Sept 2024 SpaceX signed a non-exclusive licensing agreement (USD 5M technology licence + USD 3M engineering/support). The one engine-adjacent merchant supplier with a confirmed SpaceX relationship.

metrics.description: 3D Printing Industry (citing the deal): SpaceX to pay five million dollars for Velo3D additive-manufacturing technologies; plus three million for related engineering/support (USD 8M total). Single-fact: licence portion only.

notes: Ticker VELO (Nasdaq Capital Market) verified 2026-06: re-listed 2025-08-19 after a reverse split (per Velo3D SEC 8-K/424B3 filings); appears in FY2026 filings. Confirmed SpaceX supplier of metal-AM machines used on Raptor parts. listingStatus public. NOTE financial-distress history — review listing currency at owner gate.

name: EOS GmbH (Electro Optical Systems)
description: German metal/polymer additive-manufacturing OEM; leading supplier of industrial DMLS (Direct Metal Laser Sintering, a laser powder-bed-fusion process) machines. EOS systems print rocket-engine parts across the launch industry — e.g. an ArianeGroup injector head consolidated from 247+ parts to one, and copper-alloy combustion chambers (with AMCM). Private (family/founder-owned), so no ticker.
notes: PRIVATE company (no exchange ticker — do not guess one). Merchant relevance: DMLS machines for rocket-engine injectors/combustion chambers; named users include ArianeGroup, Launcher, RUAG, Airbus D&S. SpaceX-specific use not publicly confirmed (industry-capability altitude). listingStatus private.

name: Nikon SLM Solutions AG
description: German metal additive-manufacturing OEM (Selective Laser Melting, LPBF), wholly-owned subsidiary of Nikon Corporation since Jan 2023. Supplies large-format metal 3D-printing machines (SLM-500, NXG-class) for reusable rocket engines — Rocket Lab MoU for ultra-large platforms; LEAP 71 full-flow staged-combustion (FFSC) injector heads in IN718; university reusable-engine programs with integrated cooling channels.
notes: Ownership: wholly-owned subsidiary of Nikon Corporation (Tokyo 7731.T); SLM Solutions delisted (Frankfurt) Sept 2023 after Nikon squeeze-out. Public exposure is via parent ticker 7731.T. Merchant relevance: LPBF machines for FFSC reusable rocket engines (Raptor-class cycle) — Rocket Lab/LEAP 71; SpaceX-specific use not confirmed. listingStatus subsidiary, ticker = parent.

name: Carpenter Additive (Carpenter Technology Corporation)
description: Business unit of Carpenter Technology Corporation supplying high-quality iron-, nickel-, cobalt- and titanium-based aerospace alloy metal powders for additive manufacturing. Powders feed AM rocket-engine and propulsion parts (copper alloys for combustion-chamber heat exchangers; Ni/Co superalloys for hot-section). Merchant powder tier for the engine-AM industry.
notes: Ticker CRS (NYSE) verified 2026-06 — Carpenter Additive is a business unit of Carpenter Technology Corporation (NYSE: CRS). Merchant relevance: aerospace AM metal powders (Ni/Co/Ti); GRCop copper-liner alloy on SpaceX engines is NASA-developed and largely captive, so Carpenter is mapped as industry-capability powder supplier, not a confirmed SpaceX feedstock vendor. listingStatus subsidiary (parent ticker).

name: ATI Inc. (Allegheny Technologies)
description: U.S. specialty-materials producer of titanium and titanium alloys, nickel- & cobalt-based superalloys, and metal powders (Ti, Ti-aluminides, Ni/Co superalloys) for additive manufacturing (DMLS / EBM). Supplies aerospace jet- and rocket-engine and airframe materials; merchant powder + mill-product tier for engine parts.
notes: Ticker ATI (NYSE) verified 2026-06. Merchant relevance: Ti + Ni/Co superalloy powders & mill products for aerospace engines and AM; industry-capability altitude (not a confirmed SpaceX-specific vendor). listingStatus public.

name: RBC Bearings Incorporated
description: U.S. precision-bearings manufacturer. Its Transport Dynamics FibriloidCR cryogenic self-lubricating spherical bearings/rod ends are tested and flight-proven for Space Launch Vehicle and satellite applications (-320 degF cryogenic to +450 degF); Western Precision Aero supplies gearbox/electro-mechanical gimbal assemblies for rocket thrust-vector functions. Merchant launch-vehicle bearing tier.
notes: Ticker RBC (NYSE) verified 2026-06 — RBC transferred its listing from Nasdaq to NYSE in Sept 2022, symbol unchanged 'RBC'. Merchant relevance: flight-proven cryogenic launch-vehicle bearings (FibriloidCR) + gimbal assemblies for thrust-vector. listingStatus public.

name: Aerospace aluminum-lithium plate/sheet
description: Low-density, high-stiffness aluminum-lithium (Al-Li) rolled plate, sheet and extrusions used for launch-vehicle tank barrels, domes, intertanks, stage adapters and thrust structures. Falcon 9's stage structure is an aluminum-lithium alloy; Al-Li is the merchant material tier feeding reusable-launch tankage industry-wide. Qualified Al-Li capacity is scarce enough that OEMs sign decade-long lock-ins.
notes: Industry-framed: Constellium's Airware Al-Li is supplied to Blue Origin's New Glenn launch vehicle (public). SpaceX's specific Al-Li mill supplier for Falcon 9 tankage is not publicly disclosed in reviewed sources; the merchant Al-Li tier (Constellium, Kaiser, Arconic) is the investable exposure.

name: Aerospace mill titanium (plate/bar/billet)
description: Aerospace-grade titanium mill products (plate, bar, billet, forged stock) used for reentry-control surfaces (grid fins), engine hardware and high-temperature structure. The melt/mill tier is concentrated (VSMPO-AVISMA, ATI, TIMET) and was a documented 2022 supply-risk axis after Russian titanium exposure.
notes: Concentrated melt tier; VSMPO-AVISMA (Russia) is the world's largest producer and a post-2022 export-control corner for Western buyers. ATI and TIMET (PCC) are the principal Western merchant melters. SpaceX's specific Ti mill supplier for grid-fin stock is not publicly disclosed.

name: Titanium sponge feedstock
description: Titanium sponge — the upstream feedstock from which all aerospace mill titanium is melted. A near-single-geography corner: U.S. domestic sponge production has effectively ceased, leaving Western aerospace ~import-dependent, with Japan (Osaka Titanium, Toho Titanium) the principal merchant source plus PCC/TIMET in North America.
notes: Single/near-single-geography corner: U.S. Section 232 review found only one domestic sponge producer by 2019 and ~68% sponge import reliance; Japan's two producers (Osaka, Toho) plus PCC/TIMET dominate Western-accessible sponge. Feeds the mill-titanium tier above.

name: Large aerospace titanium forgings/castings (grid fins)
description: Large single-piece titanium castings/forgings for reusable-launch reentry-control surfaces — Falcon 9's hypersonic grid fins are cast in a single piece of titanium so they survive reentry heat without shielding and are reused without per-flight replacement. The titanium cast/forged-part tier (Howmet, PCC) is a recognized aerospace capacity chokepoint.
notes: CAPTIVE CORNER: Falcon 9's titanium grid fins are cast in a single piece of titanium by SpaceX (widely reported as among the largest single-piece Ti castings); no public merchant supplier of the grid-fin casting itself is named in reviewed sources, so no supplier is invented. The merchant exposure is the large-aero-Ti-forging/casting tier generally (Howmet, PCC), and the mill-Ti and sponge feedstock above. Quote support is for the captive single-piece casting fact, not a vendor.

name: Aerospace investment castings & forgings (engine/structure)
description: High-end aerospace investment castings and structural/rotating forgings feeding rocket engines and primary structure. A roughly $10B sector dominated by a two-supplier near-duopoly (Arconic/Howmet and Precision Castparts) that is a persistent, well-known capacity chokepoint for engine and airframe production.
notes: Near-duopoly capacity corner (Howmet + PCC). Industry-framed merchant tier feeding any rocket-engine/structure program; SpaceX additively manufactures many Raptor/Merlin hot-section parts in-house (captive) — the casting/forging duopoly is exposure for the broader engine-component class, not a confirmed SpaceX BOM line.

name: Constellium
description: Constellium SE — leading aerospace aluminium producer and maker of the proprietary Airware aluminium-lithium alloy used for launch-vehicle tank and structure components. Publicly supplies Airware Al-Li plate/sheet to Blue Origin's New Glenn; merchant Al-Li exposure for reusable-launch tankage.
notes: NYSE: CSTM (verified IR/exchange this round). Aerospace/space sites at Ravenswood, WV and Issoire, France. Airware Al-Li supplied to Blue Origin New Glenn (named launch program); not a confirmed Falcon 9 BOM supplier.

name: Kaiser Aluminum
description: Kaiser Aluminum Corporation — a leading producer of semi-fabricated specialty aluminum products with a major aerospace/high-strength plate and sheet business (Trentwood, WA mill). Merchant aero-aluminum exposure; second-source candidate for aerospace Al plate.
notes: NASDAQ: KALU (verified this round). FY2024 Aerospace/High-Strength net sales reported at $883M. Trentwood expansion adds ~25% heat-treat plate capacity. Aero plate supplier; not confirmed on Falcon 9/Starship BOM.

name: Arconic
description: Arconic Corporation — major rolled-aluminum and aerospace plate/sheet producer spun from Alcoa in 2016. One of the two leading aerospace casting/structures lineages historically (the other being PCC). Taken private by Apollo Global Management in 2023.
notes: PRIVATE since H2-2023: acquired by Apollo Global Management ($30.00/share), delisted from NYSE — no active public ticker (do not assign one). Distinct from Howmet Aerospace, which also spun from Alcoa/Arconic in 2020. Merchant aero-aluminum/castings lineage; not a confirmed SpaceX supplier.

name: VSMPO-AVISMA
description: VSMPO-AVISMA Corporation — the world's largest titanium producer and historically the largest titanium supplier to Boeing and Airbus. A post-2022 export-control / sanctions corner for Western aerospace titanium; Russia-based, ~25%+1 share held by state corporation Rostec.
notes: Trades on Moscow Exchange (VSMO); not accessible to most Western investors and exposed to post-2022 sanctions. Ownership: Industrial Investments (Mikhail Shelkov) ~65.27%, Rostec 25%+1 share. World's largest Ti producer; named largest Ti supplier for Boeing commercial production. Listed honestly as the export-control corner of the mill-Ti tier, NOT as a SpaceX supplier.

name: TIMET (Titanium Metals Corp.)
description: TIMET (Titanium Metals Corporation) — integrated titanium producer (sponge, ingot, mill products) and, per its parent, the largest titanium sponge producer and melter in North America. Operated the last large U.S. sponge plant (Henderson, NV), idled since 2020. A subsidiary of Precision Castparts (Berkshire Hathaway).
notes: Subsidiary of Precision Castparts Corp. (PCC Metals Group Division), itself a Berkshire Hathaway company — public exposure only via BRK.B (parent ticker; TIMET/PCC have no standalone listing). Largest North American Ti sponge producer/melter. Held last large U.S. sponge plant (idled 2020). Upstream sponge + mill-Ti corner; not a confirmed SpaceX supplier.

name: Toho Titanium
description: Toho Titanium Co., Ltd. — one of Japan's two titanium-sponge producers (with Osaka Titanium). Together the Japanese sponge makers are the principal Western-accessible merchant source of aerospace titanium sponge feedstock as the West diversifies away from Russian supply.
notes: Tokyo Stock Exchange: 5727 (verified this round). One of only two Japanese sponge producers. NOTE: JX Advanced Metals (org_jx_advanced_metals, already in graph) announced (Feb 2026) taking Toho Titanium private via share exchange — listing status may change pending completion. Upstream sponge tier; not a confirmed SpaceX supplier. Delisted from TSE Prime 2026-05-28; wholly-owned subsidiary of JX Advanced Metals (org_jx_advanced_metals) effective 2026-06-01.

name: Osaka Titanium Technologies
description: Osaka Titanium Technologies Co., Ltd. — the world's second-largest producer of titanium sponge after VSMPO-AVISMA, and one of Japan's two sponge producers. A core merchant source of aerospace titanium sponge feedstock for Western-accessible supply.
notes: Tokyo Stock Exchange: 5726 (verified this round). Named world's second-largest titanium sponge producer after VSMPO-AVISMA. Upstream sponge tier feeding mill-Ti; not a confirmed SpaceX supplier.

name: Howmet Aerospace
description: Howmet Aerospace Inc. — leading provider of advanced engineered aerospace components: investment castings, forgings, titanium mill products/extrusions and the #1 global position in aerospace fastening systems. States it can produce more than 90% of all structural and rotating aero-engine components. One of the two dominant aerospace casting/forging producers.
notes: NYSE: HWM (verified this round). #1 global in aerospace fastening systems; produces >90% of structural/rotating aero-engine component types; Engineered Structures makes titanium ingot, mill products and forgings. One of two dominant aero casting/forging firms (with PCC). Merchant castings/forgings/Ti exposure; not a confirmed SpaceX BOM supplier.

name: Precision Castparts Corp.
description: Precision Castparts Corp. (PCC) — worldwide diversified manufacturer of complex metal components: forgings, investment castings, fasteners and airframe products for aerospace. One of the two dominant aerospace investment-casting producers and, via TIMET, the largest titanium sponge producer/melter in North America. A Berkshire Hathaway company.
notes: Acquired by Berkshire Hathaway in 2016 — public exposure only via BRK.B (no standalone listing; do not assign a PCC ticker). One of two dominant aero casting/forging firms (with Howmet). Owns TIMET (Ti sponge/mill). Merchant castings/forgings/Ti exposure; not a confirmed SpaceX BOM supplier.

name: Outokumpu
description: Outokumpu Oyj — the largest stainless-steel producer in Europe and second-largest in the Americas. Publicly reported as a supplier of stainless steel to SpaceX for Starship; merchant 300-series stainless exposure for Starship primary structure.
notes: Nasdaq Helsinki: OUT1V (verified this round). Largest stainless producer in Europe, 2nd in the Americas (Calvert, AL operations). Reported as a SpaceX Starship stainless supplier (quality secondary source); 304L is a near-commodity grade with many qualified mills, so this is illustrative merchant exposure rather than a sole-source claim.

name: Strategic radiation-hardened processor / FPGA / memory
description: The concentrated, export-sensitive corner of launch/space avionics: true rad-hard general-purpose processors, rad-hard/rad-tolerant FPGAs, and rad-hard memory for the harshest GEO/deep-space radiation environments. This is the chokepoint axis (few trusted foundries, long lead times), distinct from the COTS-upscreened path that high-cadence launchers like Falcon 9 mostly use for ascent avionics. Suppliers cluster on a handful of Western houses (BAE RAD750/RAD5545, Frontgrade/Microchip, AMD/Xilinx, plus the DoD-funded SkyWater RH90 trusted foundry).
notes: Honesty split (brief §3): this node is the STRATEGIC rad-hard corner (concentrated). Falcon 9 ascent avionics largely use COTS-upscreened silicon (commodity, broad supply) captured separately in launch_cots_upscreened_avionics_silicon. Strategic rad-hard is the corner traditional GPS/defense/GEO sat primes depend on.

name: COTS-upscreened avionics silicon (Falcon-class)
description: The commodity counterweight to strategic rad-hard: commercial-off-the-shelf silicon (e.g. dual-core x86) selected, radiation-characterized, acceptance-tested, and protected by triple modular redundancy, ECC, scrubbing, and watchdogs rather than paying the full rad-hard premium. This is how SpaceX Falcon-class ascent avionics achieves radiation tolerance with broad commercial supply, so the silicon supply here is NOT a single-source chokepoint. SpaceX's avionics design itself is captive (must_build); the underlying parts are commodity.
notes: Brief honesty call: distinguishes COTS-upscreened (commodity, broad supply, captive architecture) from strategic rad-hard (concentrated corner). Recall is NOT earned by pretending captive COTS-upscreened avionics has a public single-source supplier.

name: Space-grade IMU / inertial reference / GNSS
description: Inertial measurement / reference units (ring-laser-gyro, hemispherical-resonator-gyro, FOG, MEMS) plus GNSS receivers that feed the fault-tolerant GNC loop and the autonomous flight-safety position solution. The high-reliability space-grade IMU/gyro tier is concentrated on two dominant Western houses (Honeywell MIMU, Northrop Grumman SIRU/HRG), with Safran and Northrop-LITEF MEMS as lower-cost adjacents; modern launchers can also blend tactical-grade MEMS upscreened parts.

name: Star tracker / stellar attitude sensor
description: Optical stellar-reference sensors for precise attitude determination on upper stages, spacecraft, and (increasingly) constellation buses. The merchant star-tracker market is led by Sodern (ArianeGroup), with Jena-Optronik (Airbus) and Ball/BAE as the other established high-reliability suppliers; New Space mega-constellation demand has pulled in higher-rate, lower-cost variants. More relevant to payload/spacecraft attitude than to Falcon-9 ascent, but a core GNC sensor for the broader reusable-launch + on-orbit chain.

name: Space-grade connectors & flight harness (launch vehicle)
description: Launch-vehicle avionics interconnect: ruggedized circular/rectangular connectors, hermetics, and shielded harness rated for vibration, thermal cycling, outgassing, and radiation. Supply is broad but quality-concentrated on a few interconnect houses (Glenair, TE/DEUTSCH, Amphenol). Distinct from the orbital-data-center connector node; this is the ascent/recovery harness on the reusable stack.

name: Flight-termination ordnance & safe-and-arm devices
description: The energetic / ordnance half of the autonomous flight-safety system: safe-and-arm devices, initiators, and destruct charges that the onboard AFTS computer commands. The flight-safety DECISION computer is SpaceX-captive (custom AFTS), but the qualified safe-and-arm / ordnance hardware is a concentrated merchant corner dominated by Pacific Scientific Energetic Materials (PacSci EMC, a Fortive subsidiary), the established U.S. supplier of safe-and-arm / arm-fire devices flown on most U.S. launch vehicles.
notes: Honesty: AFTS decision/control electronics are SpaceX-captive (see autonomous_flight_safety_system + spaceflightnow AFSS evidence). The merchant exposure is the safe-and-arm / ordnance hardware, not the flight-safety software.

name: BAE Systems
description: British defense/aerospace prime and the heritage leader in strategic radiation-hardened space processors (RAD750 at 150nm, RAD5545 at 45nm; 12nm rad-hard library in development). Its single-board computers are the long-standing workhorse of high-reliability space computing. BAE also absorbed Ball Aerospace (2024) bringing the CT-2020 rad-hard star tracker. Listed on the London Stock Exchange.
notes: Strategic rad-hard processor corner. ticker BA.L verified via London Stock Exchange listing 2026-06.

name: Frontgrade Technologies
description: Self-described largest provider of analog and radiation-hardened electronics for the aerospace, defense, and medical industries; portfolio spans rad-hard FPGAs, memory, microprocessors, mission-processing subsystems, ASICs, and power management. Formerly Cobham Advanced Electronic Solutions (CAES); owned by Veritas Capital, so privately held (no public ticker).
notes: Private (Veritas Capital), formerly CAES. No public ticker; do not guess. Strategic rad-hard supplier.

name: Microchip Technology
description: U.S. semiconductor maker and one of the two dominant space-grade FPGA suppliers. Its RTG4 rad-tolerant FPGAs are hardened by design against single-event upsets for LEO/MEO/GEO/HEO/deep-space, and its RT PolarFire FPGA is QML Class Q qualified for spaceflight. Listed on Nasdaq (MCHP).
notes: ticker MCHP (Nasdaq). One of two dominant space FPGA houses (with AMD/Xilinx). Distinct company from Frontgrade despite seed lumping them.

name: AMD (Xilinx)
description: Owner of the former Xilinx space-grade FPGA line and the other of the two dominant space-FPGA suppliers. Space-grade XQR Kintex UltraScale (20nm, flying on Mars Perseverance) and the newer radiation-tolerant XQR Versal adaptive SoC (Class B qualified, shipping from early 2023, reprogrammable in-flight) anchor high-performance on-board processing. Listed on Nasdaq (AMD).
notes: ticker AMD (Nasdaq); acquired Xilinx 2022. Second of two dominant space FPGA houses.

name: SkyWater Technology
description: U.S.-owned pure-play silicon foundry and DMEA Cat-1A Trusted Foundry; recipient of DoD funding (up to $170M, then +$99M in Sept 2022) to broaden onshore production of strategic radiation-hardened (RH90, 90nm) electronics. Represents the policy-driven onshore-capacity build for the strategic rad-hard corner. Listed on Nasdaq (SKYT).
notes: ticker SKYT (Nasdaq). From .eval dev set (rl_dev_radhard_microelectronics_skywater_2019_2022). Trusted-foundry RH90 onshore capacity.

name: Northrop Grumman
description: U.S. aerospace/defense prime and the other dominant space-grade inertial house via its Scalable Space Inertial Reference Unit (SIRU) family, built on hemispherical resonator gyro (HRG) technology that has logged 50 million on-orbit hours without a single mission failure aboard more than 200 spacecraft, and is naturally radiation-hardened by its quartz construction. Its LITEF subsidiary supplies MEMS/FOG IMUs. Listed on NYSE (NOC).
notes: ticker NOC (NYSE). HRG/SIRU = second dominant space IMU/gyro corner alongside Honeywell.

name: Sodern
description: French optronics maker and self-described world leader in star trackers, offering the most extensive range on the market (Hydra, Auriga families) with extensive flight heritage from LEO to deep space; Auriga units equip large LEO communications constellations. A subsidiary of ArianeGroup (a privately held Airbus/Safran joint venture), so no public ticker of its own.
notes: Subsidiary of ArianeGroup (private Airbus/Safran JV). No standalone public ticker; do not guess. Market-leading star-tracker corner.

name: Jena-Optronik
description: German maker of star sensors / attitude-orbit-control sensors and, with Sodern, one of the two established European star-tracker houses. Its ASTRO APS is described as the world's most successful and extensively used high-reliability satellite attitude-orbit-control sensor; the compact rad-hard ASTRO CL targets small satellites and mega-constellations. A subsidiary of Airbus Defence and Space (Airbus SE, Euronext Paris AIR.PA).
notes: Subsidiary of Airbus Defence and Space; parent Airbus SE ticker AIR.PA (Euronext Paris). Second established European star-tracker house.

name: Glenair
description: U.S. interconnect maker specializing in miniaturized, weight-critical space connectors and harness. Its Series 80 Mighty Mouse is specified on hundreds of mission-critical interconnect applications worldwide and has become the de facto high-performance connector solution for former MIL-DTL-38999 users, at roughly half the size and weight. Glenair delivers complete launch-vehicle avionics interconnect systems with proven flight heritage. Privately held.
notes: Private company (no public ticker; do not guess). Concentrated launch-harness interconnect supplier.

name: Pacific Scientific Energetic Materials (PacSci EMC)
description: U.S. ordnance/energetics maker and the established supplier of safe-and-arm / arm-fire devices, initiators, and flight-termination ordnance for space launch vehicles, with hardware flown across most U.S. launch programs. A subsidiary of Ralliant Corporation (NYSE: RAL).

name: Aerospace carbon-fiber composite material (fairings & structures)
description: Aerospace-grade PAN-based carbon fiber plus matrix resin / prepreg used to build payload fairings and other composite primary structures on reusable launch vehicles. On Falcon 9 the payload fairing is a carbon fiber-aluminum honeycomb sandwich. Fairing FABRICATION is substantially captive at SpaceX (its own Hawthorne autoclaves); the MERCHANT exposure is the upstream carbon-fiber + resin material tier (Toray, Hexcel, Teijin, Mitsubishi Chemical, Syensqo). High-modulus / high-strength aerospace carbon fiber sits under a standing export-control regime (Wassenaar dual-use list; U.S. EAR/ITAR), a structural constraint on who may supply and to whom.
notes: Merchant tier = carbon-fiber + resin material; fairing lay-up/cure is captive at SpaceX. Single-/near-single-source character lives in aerospace-QUALIFIED intermediate-modulus tow, where a handful of producers (Toray, Hexcel, Teijin, Mitsubishi Chemical) are qualified into flight programs and Toray controls >50% of upstream PAN precursor. Export-control regime (Wassenaar/EAR) is a standing constraint, not a dated episode.

name: Composite-overwrapped pressure vessel (COPV) for helium pressurant
description: Composite-overwrapped pressure vessel storing high-pressure helium used to pressurize a launch vehicle's propellant tanks as engines consume propellant. Industry-standard construction is carbon-fiber composite overwrapped over a thin metal (e.g. aluminum) liner; newer Type IV/Type V designs use polymer-lined or linerless carbon overwrap. On Falcon 9 the COPVs sit inside the propellant tanks and SpaceX BUILDS ITS OWN COPVs (captive). The merchant population — Infinite Composites, Steelhead Composites, HyPerComp, General Dynamics-OTS — supplies COPVs to the broader launch / spacecraft industry and is the investable exposure for non-captive programs; the carbon-fiber overwrap itself ties back to the same aerospace carbon-fiber material tier.
notes: CAPTIVE at SpaceX (builds its own COPVs). Merchant COPV makers exist for the wider industry (Infinite Composites, Steelhead, HyPerComp, GD-OTS) and are mapped as reported_capable_supplier, not as SpaceX's manufacturer. Single-source history: the CRS-7 (2015) and AMOS-6 (2016) Falcon 9 losses both traced to COPV behavior, underscoring the qualification difficulty of this part.

name: Toray Industries
description: Japanese chemicals/materials group; the world's largest carbon fiber producer (TORAYCA brand; owns Zoltek for large-tow industrial fiber). Supplies aerospace-grade intermediate-/high-modulus carbon fiber used in commercial-aircraft primary structures and, as a material tier, in launch-vehicle composite structures (fairings) and COPV overwrap. Also dominant in the upstream PAN precursor that nearly all carbon fiber requires.

Has Pyrofil intermediate-modulus aerospace grades and is doubling carbon-fiber capacity at Tokai (Japan) and Sacramento (US) over 2025-2027 for high-end applications including aerospace. Part of the merchant aerospace carbon-fiber material tier.

Supplies aerospace-qualified epoxy resin systems and prepregs (e.g. Prism EP2400, NCAMP-qualified with Teijin Tenax fiber) plus carbon fiber for aerospace structures. Represents the resin/prepreg (matrix) half of the merchant carbon-composite material tier that feeds launch-vehicle composite structures.
notes: Holds legacy Solvay/Cytec composites business post Dec-2023 spin-off; aerospace-qualified resin/prepreg (Prism EP2400, NCAMP). Listed Euronext Brussels SYENS (ISIN BE0003851681) — verified this round; do NOT attribute to legacy Solvay ticker. Resin/matrix-tier reported_capable_supplier.

name: Infinite Composites
description: U.S. (Tulsa, OK) maker of linerless (Type V) composite pressure vessels and COPVs for pressurant and propellant tanks in launch vehicles, satellites, lunar landers and space fueling depots. Private company; government/research customers shown include NASA, U.S. Air Force, U.S. Army. Represents the merchant COPV population that non-captive launch programs can buy (SpaceX itself builds COPVs in-house).
notes: Private; merchant COPV / linerless CPV maker for launch vehicles & spacecraft. No verified ticker (private) — not guessed. reported_capable_supplier to the COPV component (SpaceX COPV is captive).

name: Steelhead Composites
description: U.S. (Golden, CO) maker of high-performance COPVs integrated into launch-vehicle propulsion systems and used as primary/auxiliary tanks for spacecraft propulsion, with liners selected for hypergolic, cryogenic or pressurized-gas propellant compatibility. Private company; part of the merchant COPV population for the broader launch/space industry.
notes: Private; merchant COPV maker for launch-vehicle propulsion & spacecraft. No verified ticker (private) — not guessed. reported_capable_supplier to the COPV component.

name: HyPerComp Engineering
description: U.S. (Brigham City, UT) developer, qualifier and producer of composite-overwrapped pressure vessels (COPVs); AS9100-D, products used in space launch vehicles among other applications. Co-developed a Type IV carbon-overwrap COPV with Hexcel using HexTow IM11-R/12K carbon fiber for aerospace and space. Private company; part of the merchant COPV population.
notes: Private (founded 1996, <20 employees, AS9100-D); merchant COPV maker for space launch vehicles. No verified ticker (private). reported_capable_supplier; also links the carbon-fiber tier (Hexcel HexTow IM11-R) into COPV overwrap.

name: General Dynamics Ordnance and Tactical Systems
description: Composite-structures unit (Lincoln Operations) of General Dynamics (NYSE: GD). Design authority for the NASA SLS Core Stage and Upper Stage COPVs and for multiple satellite COPVs that provide compressed gas for propulsion subsystems; applications also include launch-vehicle and satellite propulsion. Listed via parent General Dynamics. Part of the merchant COPV population (SLS, satellites — not SpaceX, which is captive).

name: Helium pressurant supply
description: Merchant liquid/gaseous helium used to pressurize ground and flight fluid systems, purge propellant lines, and provide cryogenic cool-down for reusable-launch operations. It is the most supply-concentrated propellant-lane input: helium is a by-product of a handful of natural-gas fields and a small set of producers, and it is periodically short, so launch operators must secure dedicated supply (e.g. the NASA-Air Products sole-source liquid-helium contract for KSC/Cape Canaveral).

metrics.name: US helium use in aerospace, pressurizing and purging
metrics.description: USGS Mineral Commodity Summaries 2024 (helium): of estimated US Grade-A and gaseous helium apparent consumption in 2023, 'aerospace, pressuring, and purging' accounted for 9%. Demand-side end-use share, not a launch-specific figure.

metrics.name: US helium import sources (2019-22)
metrics.description: USGS Mineral Commodity Summaries 2024 (helium): US import sources 2019-2022. Illustrates how geographically concentrated merchant helium supply is.

notes: Single/near-single-source corner of the propellants lane: helium is a periodically-short, by-product commodity concentrated in a few fields (US + Qatar dominant) and a handful of producers. The 2022 episode (NASA's $1.07B sole-source liquid-helium award to Air Products for KSC launch operations) is the canonical chokepoint. Reusable-launch operators draw on the same concentrated merchant network.

name: Liquid oxygen (LOX) supply
description: Merchant liquid oxygen used as the oxidizer for both kerolox (Falcon 9 / Merlin) and methalox (Starship / Raptor) reusable-launch propellant systems. LOX is produced by cryogenic air separation; the merchant supply is an oligopoly of industrial-gas majors. For high-cadence reusable launch the binding constraint is dedicated air-separation capacity and cryogenic-tanker delivery sited near the launch site, which is why Linde is building/operating dedicated air-separation units at Brownsville (Starbase) and Mims, Florida (Cape-area launches).
notes: Genuinely merchant tier. Named supplier where a specific contract exists: Linde (dedicated Brownsville ASU for SpaceX Starbase; Mims, FL plant for a 'major space launch company' in Florida). Air Liquide is a supplemental/historical KSC supplier. The 2021 COVID LOX shortage (dev set rl_dev_lox_covid_shortage_2021) hit the shared merchant LOX supply/delivery network rather than one named producer.

name: Liquid methane (LCH4) supply
description: Rocket-grade liquid methane (LCH4) used as the fuel for the methalox Starship/Super Heavy reusable system. Unlike LOX and helium, methane is not an air-separation product: SpaceX buys liquefied natural gas (LNG, predominantly methane) and purifies/conditions it to rocket-grade, drawing on the natural-gas / LNG merchant network (LNG terminals near Brownsville) rather than the industrial-gas majors. This is a distinct supply chain (cryogenic natural-gas liquefaction and trucking) and is comparatively less concentrated, though rocket-grade purity and cryogenic-tanker logistics still gate cadence.
notes: Distinct merchant network from LOX/helium: LNG/natural-gas, not air separation. No single industrial-gas major is the named methane producer; SpaceX sources purified LNG from the natural-gas supply chain (Brownsville LNG terminals nearby) and has at times signaled intent to produce its own. Grey-tier pointers (blogs) name a logistics carrier 'GenOx' for liquid-methane trucking to Boca Chica and Air Liquide for LOX, but these are not quality sources for a supplier claim and are intentionally not modeled as named-supplier edges here. Left as a decomposition frontier for the upstream pass (round 2) to resolve the rocket-grade LNG producers/conditioners.

name: Air Products and Chemicals, Inc.
description: US-headquartered (Allentown, PA) industrial-gas major; one of the big-five global industrial-gas producers and a leading helium supplier to the space-launch industry. Awarded NASA's sole-source liquid-helium supply contract (33 million liters, ~$1.07B) for Kennedy Space Center / Cape Canaveral launch operations, including its proprietary liquid-helium pumps.
notes: Investor relevance: most direct public exposure to launch-grade helium supply (the propellant lane's tightest corner). Helium is a small slice of APD revenue, so exposure is thematic not material; ticker APD verified on NYSE this round.

name: Nippon Sanso Holdings Corporation (Matheson)
description: Japan-headquartered industrial-gas major (formerly Taiyo Nippon Sanso); fourth/fifth-largest global industrial-gas group, majority-owned by Mitsubishi Chemical Group. Its US operating company is Matheson Tri-Gas (Irving, TX). Describes itself as one of only a handful of global helium producers and suppliers, with owned helium-source rights and long-term supply contracts.
notes: Reported-capable helium/industrial-gas supplier to the launch merchant network (not a confirmed SpaceX-specific contract). One of the 'handful' of global helium producers, so relevant to the concentrated-helium-corner story. Ticker 4091.T verified on Tokyo Stock Exchange this round (parent Mitsubishi Chemical Group holds majority).

name: Messer SE & Co. KGaA
description: German family-owned industrial-gas group; describes itself as the largest privately held industrial-gas company in the world and a leading industrial/medical gas company across the Americas, Asia and Europe. In June 2024 it completed the acquisition of the US Federal Helium System (Cliffside Field, reserve, and 423-mile crude-helium pipeline) from the BLM, strengthening its domestic helium position. Long-term minority shareholder is GIC.
notes: Private (no ticker) per ADR-0009 honesty rule — do NOT assign one. Strategically important to the helium corner because it now owns/operates the Cliffside Federal Helium System, a major US crude-helium source. Models the concentrated-helium-supply structure even though investors cannot hold it directly; minority partner GIC.

name: PICA-class ablative heat-shield material
description: Phenolic Impregnated Carbon Ablator (PICA)-class low-density ablative thermal-protection material — the heritage reusable/entry-vehicle heatshield basis for capsules and entry systems. Built from a carbon FiberForm preform (made from a rayon/Lyocell carbon precursor) impregnated with phenolic resin. Distinct from Starship's reusable silica ceramic tiles, but the same supply tier (carbon precursor -> preform) is the documented thermal-protection chokepoint for the U.S. reusable-launch / entry-vehicle base.
notes: [structural-deepening 2026-06-16] re-homed for render via `requires` from starship_ship_reusable_upper_stage (depth-4 lift); tagged key as the Starship-reuse TPS frontier. part_of to the tile system preserved.

name: PICA rayon / Lyocell carbon precursor
description: Cellulosic carbon precursor fiber (non-woven rayon, now domestic Lyocell) that is carbonized into the FiberForm preform inside PICA-class ablators. This is the documented single/near-single-source corner: the heritage NASA-qualified rayon supplier (SNIACE, Spain) ceased production, forcing repeated requalification and a NASA-driven switch to a domestic Lyocell precursor (PICA-D). The single hardest-to-second-source item in the ablative-TPS chain.
notes: Documented chokepoint (dev set rl_dev_pica_rayon_precursor_sole_source). Heritage rayon (SNIACE) is the historic sole-qualified precursor that ceased; domestic Lyocell replacement precursor is supplied by Lenzing AG (LENZING Lyocell). Rayon no longer a viable process in US/Europe for environmental reasons, removing alternative rayon sources.

name: PICA carbon FiberForm preform
description: Low-density carbon-fiber 'FiberForm' preform — the rigid carbonized cellulosic-fiber matrix that, once impregnated with phenolic, becomes a PICA-class ablator. Made by Fiber Materials Inc (FMI, Biddeford ME); NASA Ames worked with FMI to upgrade facilities to make an aerospace-grade FiberForm from the Lyocell precursor (PICA-D). A near-single-source aerospace preform tier feeding entry-vehicle heatshields.
notes: FMI is the named FiberForm preform maker (Steve Violette, FMI, is a co-author on NASA's PICA-sustainment papers). FMI acquired by Spirit AeroSystems 2020, sold to Tex Tech Industries (private) Jan 2025 for $165M.

name: Reusable ceramic / silica heat-shield tile
description: Rigid high-purity silica/ceramic reusable surface-insulation tile (Shuttle-heritage LI-900/LI-2200 class; Starship hexagonal silica ceramic tile). The reusable counterpart to ablative PICA: meant for repeated reentry without replacement. For Starship specifically this tile is SpaceX-CAPTIVE — produced in-house at SpaceX's tile 'bakery' (Roberts Road), not bought from a merchant tile maker — so genuine merchant exposure here is thin. Heritage industry tile maker was Lockheed Missiles & Space (LI-900).
notes: CAPTIVE call: Starship tiles are made in-house by SpaceX; no public merchant silica supplier is named for Starship. Merchant tier shown here is the heritage Shuttle-class tile maker (Lockheed Martin, LI-900) for industry framing, not a verified Starship supplier. name: High-temp TPS tile adhesive & strain-isolator pad
description: High-temperature room-temperature-vulcanizing (RTV) silicone tile adhesive plus the Nomex-felt strain-isolator pad (SIP) that decouples a rigid TPS tile from the vehicle's structural deflection. Shuttle-heritage stack: RTV-560 silicone bonds the tile to a Nomex felt SIP, which bonds to the airframe. Merchant materials exist (silicone RTV; aramid felt), but Starship's specific tile-attachment method is SpaceX-defined and not publicly sourced to these vendors.
notes: Industry merchant material tier (RTV silicone + aramid felt SIP). RTV-560 historically made by GE, now Momentive Performance Materials (KCC-owned); Nomex felt is a DuPont aramid. These are reported_capable industry materials, NOT verified as Starship's bonding suppliers (Starship tile attach is captive).

name: Lenzing AG
description: Austrian cellulosic-fiber producer; maker of LENZING / TENCEL Lyocell. Its Lyocell fiber is the domestic-replacement carbon precursor for NASA's PICA-D ablative heatshields (low alkaline-metal content makes it suitable as a carbon-fiber precursor). The publicly investable face of the otherwise sole-source PICA precursor corner.
notes: Lyocell precursor for PICA-D heatshields. Listed on Vienna Stock Exchange (Wiener Borse), ISIN AT0000644505. Ticker verified on exchange page this round.

name: Fiber Materials Inc (FMI)
description: Biddeford, Maine high-temperature carbon/carbon and reinforced-composites maker; produces the low-density carbon FiberForm preform used in PICA-class ablators, plus re-entry nose tips and rocket-motor throats/nozzles. NASA Ames partnered with FMI to make aerospace-grade FiberForm from the Lyocell precursor (PICA-D). The near-single-source aerospace preform supplier.
notes: FMI acquired by Spirit AeroSystems Jan 2020 ($120M); sold to Tex Tech Industries (private) Jan 2025 ($165M). No public ticker — owned by private Tex Tech. (Spirit AeroSystems itself is being acquired by Boeing, but FMI left Spirit before that closed.)

name: Lockheed Martin
description: U.S. aerospace/defense prime; Lockheed Missiles & Space Company (Sunnyvale CA) developed and manufactured the Shuttle's LI-900 / LI-2200 reusable silica surface-insulation tiles (99.9% pure silica glass fibers). Heritage merchant maker of reusable ceramic TPS tiles — industry reference point for the reusable-tile tier (Starship's own tiles are captive).
notes: Heritage Shuttle LI-900 tile maker; reported_capable for reusable ceramic TPS tiles, NOT a verified Starship supplier. NYSE: LMT (established listing).

name: Momentive Performance Materials
description: Global high-performance silicones maker; supplies RTV silicones for aerospace thermal-protection systems (cast-in-place heat shielding, thermal-blanket adhesion). Maker of the RTV-560-class red phenyl-methyl silicone historically used to bond Shuttle TPS tiles to strain-isolator pads. Industry RTV-adhesive tier for the tile-bonding process.
notes: Fully acquired by KCC Corporation (Seoul-listed) 2024-05-14; Momentive itself is private. KCC parent ticker NOT verified this round -> no ticker recorded (no guess). reported_capable industry RTV-adhesive supplier, not a verified Starship supplier.

name: SNIACE S.A.
description: Spanish specialty-cellulose and viscose/rayon producer (Torrelavega). Was NASA's qualified non-domestic rayon supplier for the PICA carbon precursor; its rayon was carbonized into FiberForm for PICA heatshields. Ceased rayon/viscose production and entered liquidation, breaking the heritage PICA precursor supply chain and triggering the NASA Lyocell (PICA-D) substitution.
notes: Historic sole-qualified PICA rayon precursor supplier that ceased production — the root of the documented chokepoint. Formerly Madrid-listed; liquidated ~2020 -> treated as private/defunct, no current ticker (no guess).

name: Flight computer / integrated avionics box (merchant tier)
description: The integrated flight-control computer / avionics unit that runs guidance, navigation and control and sequences the vehicle. SpaceX builds its Falcon and Starship flight computers in-house around triple-redundant, radiation-tolerant-by-architecture compute, but a genuine merchant tier serves the broader (non-vertically-integrated) reusable-launch industry: Beyond Gravity (RUAG Space), Innoflight, Moog and Airbus Defence/BAE supply launch- and spacecraft-class avionics boxes. Mapped as the industry chain a program that does not build its own avionics would procure, not a confirmed SpaceX purchase.
notes: Captive-vs-merchant honesty (scope §1): SpaceX flight computers are in-house (triple-redundant COTS-upscreened compute). The named merchant suppliers fly avionics boxes on other launch/space programs and represent the buyable tier for a non-captive reusable-launch program. Qualitative industry-capability mapping, not a verified SpaceX supply relationship.

name: Flight power distribution unit & battery (merchant tier)
description: Power conditioning / distribution electronics and flight batteries (typically lithium-ion) that supply the avionics, actuators and pyrotechnics through ascent and recovery. The merchant tier is well established: EaglePicher and Saft (TotalEnergies) are the dominant Western space-battery houses, with Vicor and Crane Aerospace supplying high-density power-conversion modules. SpaceX integrates its own power electronics, so this is the industry-chain tier a non-captive program buys.
notes: Industry-chain mapping (scope §1): named space-battery / power-module suppliers serve launch and satellite programs broadly; their specific role on SpaceX vehicles is not publicly confirmed and is treated as qualitative industry capability.

name: RF telemetry / command transponder (merchant tier)
description: S-band / X-band telemetry, tracking and command transponders and transmitters that carry vehicle telemetry to the range and receive command / flight-termination uplinks. A constrained, qualification-heavy merchant tier: L3Harris, Safran Data Systems (formerly Zodiac/Cobham), and Quasonix supply launch-range telemetry hardware. Relevant both to range communications and to the command link feeding the flight-safety system.
notes: Industry-chain mapping (scope §1): qualified telemetry/transponder suppliers serve the launch-range community broadly; specific SpaceX usage is not publicly confirmed and is treated as qualitative industry capability.

name: Fairing composite sandwich panel (CFRP / aluminum-honeycomb)
description: The large carbon-fiber-reinforced-polymer face-sheet over aluminum-honeycomb sandwich half-shell that forms the payload fairing. Reusing a fairing requires the panel to survive ascent loads, reentry heating and saltwater immersion, then be refurbished — a real fabrication frontier for large, thin, autoclave- or out-of-autoclave-cured composite shells. Merchant aerostructure fabricators (Beyond Gravity / RUAG, which makes Atlas and Ariane fairings; Spirit AeroSystems composites) define the industry tier; SpaceX fabricates Falcon fairings in-house.
notes: Tagged key as a genuine large-CFRP-shell fabrication frontier (reuse adds reentry + saltwater survival). Upstream carbon-fiber/prepreg supply (Toray, Hexcel, Teijin) is already in the graph and should be reused rather than re-added; merchant fairing fabricators (Beyond Gravity, Spirit) are the structural tier.

name: Fairing recovery cold-gas RCS / guided-parafoil system
description: The cold-gas attitude-control thrusters plus steerable parafoil that orient each fairing half after separation and guide it to a controlled water or ship-borne recovery — the hardware that turned the fairing from an expendable into a reused component. Guided-parafoil systems are a named merchant tier (Airborne Systems); cold-gas thruster modules come from suppliers such as Moog and Bradford. SpaceX integrates the recovery system on Falcon fairings.
notes: Recovery hardware is qualitatively grounded in public Falcon fairing-recovery coverage (cold-gas reorientation + parafoil descent). Merchant parafoil/thruster suppliers serve the broader industry; specific SpaceX supply is not publicly confirmed.

name: Fairing separation pneumatic pusher system
description: The low-shock pneumatic pusher / separation mechanism that splits and pushes apart the two fairing halves at jettison. Falcon 9 uses a pneumatic (rather than purely pyrotechnic) fairing-separation system to reduce shock and avoid debris — a deliberately reuse- and payload-friendly design choice. A distinct mechanism from the recovery cold-gas/parafoil hardware that acts after separation.
notes: Grounded in public description of Falcon 9's pneumatic (low-shock, all-pneumatic) fairing-separation system. Distinct hardware from fairing_recovery_rcs_cold_gas (separation event vs post-separation descent control); kept as separate genuine subsystems, not a split of one thing.

name: Reaction-control cold-gas / monopropellant thruster set (merchant tier)
description: Small attitude-control thrusters used by the upper stage for coast-phase reorientation, settling burns and pointing. SpaceX's Falcon upper stage uses an in-house cold-gas (nitrogen) RCS and Draco-class monopropellant thrusters; the genuine merchant tier — Moog, Aerojet Rocketdyne (L3Harris) MR-series, Bradford ECAPS, ArianeGroup — supplies equivalent thruster sets to the broader launch and spacecraft industry.
notes: Captive-vs-merchant honesty (scope §1): SpaceX upper-stage RCS is in-house (cold-gas N2 + Draco). Merchant thruster suppliers fly on other programs and represent the buyable tier for a non-captive reusable program; qualitative industry mapping.

name: Interstage & stage-separation structure
description: The composite interstage that connects the booster and second stage and houses the stage-separation system. On Falcon 9 the interstage carries the pneumatic stage-separation pushers and the booster-side mounting for grid fins, and must release cleanly at separation while surviving booster reentry for reuse. A distinct structural/mechanism subsystem from the engines it sits between.
notes: Grounded in public Falcon 9 architecture (composite interstage, pneumatic pusher separation, grid-fin mounting). Reuse-relevant because the booster-side interstage region must survive entry. Carbon-fiber supply already modeled upstream; not re-added here.

name: Grid-fin hydraulic actuation system (merchant tier)
description: The hydraulic actuators and power pack that deploy and articulate the titanium grid fins to steer the booster during reentry and descent. Falcon 9's grid fins are hydraulically actuated; the actuation hardware is genuinely distinct from engine-gimbal thrust-vector-control actuators (different loads, duty cycle and mounting). Merchant hydraulic-actuation suppliers (Moog, Woodward, Parker Hannifin) define the industry tier.
notes: Kept distinct from launch_tvc_actuators_merchant on purpose: grid-fin reentry-control hydraulics and engine-gimbal TVC are genuinely separate hardware (different parts, specs, environment) — not one real thing split in two. Grounded in public Falcon 9 grid-fin hydraulic actuation.

name: Landing-leg crushable aluminum-honeycomb core
description: The one-shot crushable aluminum-honeycomb energy absorber inside the landing legs that dissipates touchdown energy by plastically deforming. As a single-use consumable it is the leg's reuse-limiting element (replaced between flights), distinct from the carbon-fiber/aluminum telescoping leg structure itself. Crushable aluminum-honeycomb absorbers are a real merchant material tier (Hexcel, Plascore, Argosy).
notes: ADR-0005 override basis: Falcon legs are mature/widely-adopted, so this passes as a reuse-CONSUMABLE story (the crushable core is spent per landing), not as a supply chokepoint. Kept to ONE node — a mature leg is not over-decomposed. Tagged key to render as the reuse-limiting consumable.

name: COPV metallic liner (thin Inconel / titanium)
description: The thin gas-tight metallic liner inside the carbon-overwrapped pressure vessels (COPVs) that store high-pressure helium for tank pressurization. Liner integrity and the liner/overwrap/propellant interface were central to the Falcon 9 AMOS-6 (2016) on-pad failure investigation, making the liner a documented failure-mode chokepoint. Merchant COPV / liner makers (Infinite Composites, Steelhead Composites, HyPerComp Engineering) define the industry tier.
notes: Depth note: the COPV vessel node itself sits at canvas depth 4 (a child of it would be clipped), so the liner is wired as a sibling under the tank structure (depth 3 -> liner renders at depth 4). Tagged key as a documented AMOS-6 failure-mode chokepoint. Merchant COPV/liner orgs already in the exposure file.

name: Aerospace stainless-steel coil/plate (304L / 30X-class)
description: The stainless-steel mill product (coil and plate) that SpaceX rolls, forms and welds into Starship and Super Heavy tank barrels and domes. SpaceX moved from 301/304L stainless to a proprietary in-house alloy it calls 30X to improve cryogenic strength and reusability. The merchant mill tier — Outokumpu, North American Stainless / Acerinox, ArcelorMittal stainless — supplies the base coil/plate; the 30X composition is SpaceX-proprietary.
notes: Fills the explicit frontier flagged in the parent starship_stainless_steel_primary_structure description ('exact alloy/process details remain outside this first pass'). 30X is SpaceX-proprietary; the buyable base is mill stainless from Outokumpu (already in the exposure file) and peers. Tagged key as the structural material frontier.

name: Starship header tanks (landing-propellant storage)
description: The smaller header tanks that store the dedicated methane and oxygen used for Starship's landing burn, isolated from the main tanks so settled, conditioned propellant is available for the flip-and-land maneuver. The methane header sits in the nosecone with a downcomer through the main tank; this propellant-management architecture is a distinctive reuse-enabling subsystem of the Starship upper stage.
notes: Grounded in publicly documented Starship header-tank architecture (nose methane header + downcomer; separate landing-propellant tanks). Distinctive reuse subsystem of the ship stage, not a generic tank.

name: Radiatively-cooled niobium-alloy nozzle extension
description: The large radiation-cooled columbium (niobium alloy, typically C-103) nozzle skirt fitted to vacuum-optimized upper-stage engines, where the thin refractory-metal extension runs red-hot and radiates heat rather than being regeneratively cooled. C-103 nozzle extensions are standard on vacuum engines across the industry (e.g. RL10-class). The niobium feedstock itself is a textbook supply chokepoint — a single producer (CBMM, Brazil) accounts for the large majority of world niobium.
notes: Mapped as the INDUSTRY vacuum-engine nozzle tier (scope §1): radiation-cooled C-103 extensions are standard on vac engines; whether Merlin Vacuum specifically uses a niobium extension is not asserted here. Tagged key on the genuine niobium feedstock-concentration chokepoint (CBMM dominant); refractory-metal fabricators (e.g. ATI) are the merchant tier.

name: Flame deflector & water-deluge sound-suppression system
description: The steel flame deflector and high-volume water-deluge system that protects the pad surface and suppresses the acoustic and overpressure energy at ignition and liftoff. After Starship's first integrated flight (April 2023) cratered the Starbase pad, SpaceX built a water-cooled steel deluge plate and large water system beneath the orbital launch mount — a genuine, documented ground subsystem that gates launch cadence and pad survivability.
notes: Grounded in public post-mishap documentation of the Starbase water-deluge / steel-plate system. Exposure is thin: this is mostly bespoke civil/steel and water-system work rather than a named merchant component tier — noted honestly, no invented suppliers.

name: Cryogenic propellant storage & transfer tank farm
description: The ground tank farm of large liquid-oxygen and (for Starship) liquid-methane storage tanks, plus transfer lines and pumps that feed the pad. Tank-farm sizing, replenishment and chilldown drive turnaround time and launch cadence for a high-flight-rate reusable program. Cryogenic storage tanks and equipment are a named merchant tier (Chart Industries, Linde Engineering, Air Products).
notes: Cryo storage/transfer equipment has a real merchant tier (Chart, Linde, Air Products); org_linde already exists cross-domain and should be reused rather than re-added in the later exposure pass.

name: Propellant subcooler / densification skid
description: The ground subcooling / densification skid that chills liquid oxygen (and on Falcon 9, RP-1) below its normal boiling point to increase propellant density, letting the vehicle load more mass into a fixed tank volume. Densified-propellant loading is a defining feature of Falcon 9 Full Thrust and feeds directly into the late-load cryogenic sequence. A distinct ground subsystem below the storage tank farm.
notes: Grounded in publicly documented SpaceX subcooled/densified propellant loading (Falcon 9 Full Thrust). Sits below the cryo tank farm as the densification stage feeding the late-load sequence. Cryogenic refrigeration/subcooler equipment overlaps the Linde/Chart industrial-gas tier.

name: GSE umbilical & quick-disconnect plate
description: The ground-support umbilical lines and quick-disconnect (QD) plates that carry propellant, pressurant, purge gas, power and data to the vehicle on the pad and release cleanly at launch. On Starbase the booster and ship QD plates on the tower (and the tower's stage-0 umbilicals) are reuse-critical interfaces that must mate and demate reliably every flight. A distinct ground/interface subsystem from the storage and deluge systems.
notes: Grounded in publicly documented Starbase tower quick-disconnect / umbilical interfaces (booster + ship QD arms, stage-0 umbilicals). Largely bespoke ground hardware; merchant exposure is thin and noted honestly.

name: Starship flap electric actuator (high-power EMA)
description: The battery-powered electromechanical actuators that drive Starship's forward and aft reentry flaps during the bellyflop descent and flip. SpaceX has publicly stated Starship uses Tesla-derived electric motors and battery packs for flap (and engine) actuation, replacing the hydraulics used on earlier vehicles — a distinctive all-electric control-surface actuation approach. Largely captive (Tesla/SpaceX in-house); the high-power EMA merchant tier (Moog, Collins) is only a substitution reference.
notes: Captive call (scope §1): Starship flap/engine actuation is in-house Tesla-derived electric (publicly stated by SpaceX/Musk), so merchant exposure is thin. Kept as a structural decomposition node labeled captive; no merchant supplier invented.

name: Starship hot-stage separation ring
description: The vented interstage ring atop Super Heavy that enables hot-staging — igniting the ship's engines while still attached so their exhaust vents through the ring as the stages separate. Added to the Starship architecture after Flight 1 and revised for reuse (initially expendable, later retained on the booster), it is a distinctive, publicly documented structural subsystem of the Super Heavy / Starship separation event.
notes: Grounded in publicly documented Starship hot-staging ring (introduced for Flight 2; later iterations retained on the booster for reuse). Distinctive separation-system structure, not a generic interstage.

name: Innoflight, Inc.
description: U.S. (San Diego, California) space-avionics firm (founded 2004) making compact flight computers and integrated avionics for launch and spacecraft — its CFC-400X compact flight computer was selected by L3Harris for the Space Development Agency Tracking Layer program. Privately held (no public ticker). A merchant flight-computer tier supplier for non-captive reusable-launch / space programs.
notes: PRIVATE (no ticker; confirmed not listed via PitchBook/Crunchbase/ZoomInfo profiles). Real merchant compact flight computer (CFC-400X) with named customers (L3Harris SDA Tracking Layer, Northrop). Not a SpaceX-confirmed supplier -> reported_capable_supplier. Country: USA.

description: Swiss/Sweden-headquartered space supplier (formerly RUAG Space; part of RUAG International Holding AG), 100% owned by the Swiss Confederation (privatization targeted mid-term, not listed). A marquee merchant supplier of launch-vehicle avionics AND payload fairings — it supplies fairings on European Ariane and Vega rockets and many U.S. ULA rockets. Industry-chain capability exposure for non-captive reusable-launch programs.
notes: STATE-OWNED (100% Swiss Confederation), not listed -> no ticker. Strong merchant position in launch avionics AND payload fairings (links both the flight-computer and fairing-panel components). Capability/industry-chain exposure, not a SpaceX supplier. Country: Switzerland/Sweden.

description: U.S. (Joplin, Missouri) space-and-defense battery maker; the strongest U.S. space-battery name, having supplied batteries for a very large share of U.S. space missions (Mars rovers, Hubble, ISS, launch vehicles). Privately held — owned by Tuthill Corporation since October 2023 (prior GTCR private equity), so no public ticker. Merchant flight-battery tier for non-captive launch programs.

description: French multi-energy major (Paris-headquartered) and parent of Saft Groupe, which makes space- and aviation-grade lithium-ion batteries. Reported at roughly 75–82% of the world niobium market, with Brazil supplying about 90% of global niobium production (USGS). Privately held (Moreira Salles family ~70%, Japanese/Korean consortium ~15%, Chinese consortium ~15%) — no public ticker. The single strongest verified chokepoint in this exposure plan, though non-investable directly.
